label: In potency / mutable
term: in potency / mutable (aliquo modo in potentia)
resolution: Q.9 a.2 distinguishes mutability through potency in the subject (DEF-POTENCY) from mutability through a power in another (DEF-MUTABLE-THROUGH-ANOTHER), such as the creator's power to withhold esse. STMT-SUCCESSION-REQUIRES-POTENCY, STMT-LIFE-BOUNDARY-REQUIRES-POTENCY, STMT-PURE-ACT-LIVES and STMT-IMMUTABLE-IS-BOETHIAN-ETERNAL all use only potency in the subject, the InPotency that PureAct quantifies over. The derivation does not pass to the wider sense: it neither shows that what lacks subject potency is unconservable nor that external dependence is excluded. The boundary premise is exactly where the wider sense would intrude: q.10 a.1 gives only that what begins is not altogether immutable.
